description: Phase-FIX — UX error-message hardening. 4 stories targeting two generic fallback strings that hide diagnostic context today: 'Sorry, I couldn't process your message. Please try again.' (loop.go:336 + telegram/chat_client.go:59,63) and 'I reached the per-turn budget without a usable result.' (loop_dedup.go:79, emitted on MaxElapsed/empty-LLM/MaxIterations-without-finalize). userStories.title: Diagnostic LLM-error class in user-visible message
userStories.description: Replace the two 'Sorry, I couldn't process your message. Please try again.' emission sites with a diagnostic message that includes error class (rate-limited / network / model-error / auth-error / unknown) + a one-line retry hint. Reuse the existing `internal/llm.Classify(err)` (retry.go:81) which already returns BucketPermanent | BucketTransient | BucketContent buckets + a cleaned string. Add a new helper `internal/llm/usererror.go` exposing `func UserMessageFor(err error) string` that maps the bucket + a finer sub-classification (HTTP 429 vs network timeout vs auth-failure vs model-not-found) to a short user-facing string + hint. NEVER leak err.Error() raw to the user (provider headers, tokens, URLs may appear there) -- only the classified label + a fixed hint string. Then update internal/agent/loop.go:336 and internal/channels/telegram/chat_client.go:59-63 to call the helper. Telemetry: keep err logged at warn level (already happens via existing logger.Warn calls); the change is user-facing only.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/llm/usererror.go created (or merged into existing classify.go if cleaner) exposing UserMessageFor(err error) string

Mapping covers at minimum: rate-limited (HTTP 429 / 'rate' substring in transient bucket) -> 'Aura is rate-limited by the LLM provider. Retrying automatically did not recover -- try again in ~30s.'; network/transient -> 'Network issue talking to the LLM. Try again.'; auth (HTTP 401/403) -> 'LLM auth failed -- check API key in /settings.'; model error (HTTP 404 / 'model' in permanent) -> 'LLM model unavailable -- check model name in /settings.'; unknown -> 'Aura could not reach the LLM. Try again.'

userStories.title: Audit retry wiring + Stream-path coverage + 429 retry test
userStories.description: Retry is ALREADY wired in cmd/aura/helpers.go:64 via llm.NewRetryClient wrapping the OpenAI client at construction time. agent.ChatClient is the noStreamClient adapter (internal/agent/no_stream_client.go:31) that calls llm.Client.Send -- so every loop.go `client.Chat()` call benefits automatically. This story is AUDIT + COVERAGE, not new wiring. Steps: (1) Grep + verify the path: confirm cmd/aura/helpers.go:64 is the only construction site used in production (vs debug_llm); confirm telegram channel uses the same wrapped client (it should -- it goes through the same agentloop). (2) Read internal/llm/retry.go Stream() -- already implemented at retry.go:116 but verify it is the path Telegram streaming uses (chat_client.go uses streaming). If Telegram bypasses Stream wrapping, that is the bug to fix. (3) Add unit test in internal/llm/retry_test.go: simulate inner client returning HTTP 429 on first call + 200 on second -> assert retry kicks in + jittered backoff observed (mock time or assert callCount). (4) Add probe_chat case (in cmd/probe_chat/cases.go) that forces a transient failure path and verifies the response is not the fallback string. (5) Document the retry config knobs (MaxRetries=5, BaseDelay=1s, MaxDelay=30s from DefaultRetryConfig) in a short comment block above helpers.go:64. If the audit reveals Telegram bypasses the wrapper (Caso B), fix the construction site too.

userStories.title: Graceful finalize on ALL budget paths (MaxElapsed + empty-LLM + MaxIterations)
userStories.description: Today `finalizeAnswerAfterBudget` (loop.go:649) is called only from the MaxIterations exit path (loop.go:637) and gated by AllowNoToolFinalization. Three other budget paths emit the generic 'I reached the per-turn budget without a usable result.' string directly via `finalAnswerOnBudget(lastToolResult)`: (a) MaxElapsed loop.go:267; (b) empty-LLM-response no-tool-calls loop.go:354-357; (c) MaxIterations fallback when AllowNoToolFinalization is false or the finalize round itself fails loop.go:643. Story: extract a single helper `gracefulFinalize(ctx, client, state, opts, stats, lastToolResult, stopReason)` that wraps the existing `finalizeAnswerAfterBudget` call + falls back to `finalAnswerOnBudget` if the finalize round returns false. Wire it into all 3 paths (MaxElapsed, empty-LLM, MaxIterations) -- preserving the existing AllowNoToolFinalization gate (only call the LLM-round helper when the flag is true, but ALWAYS pass through the helper so logging + telemetry are uniform). Add a new `stats.StopReason = 'empty_llm_response'` for path (b). Verify `cmd/aura/web_chat.go:162` (and Telegram path) already set AllowNoToolFinalization: true -- extend coverage if not.
acceptanceCriteria: New helper in internal/agent/loop.go `gracefulFinalize(...)` that encapsulates: AllowNoToolFinalization -> try finalizeAnswerAfterBudget; on success return text + stats updated; on failure or flag false return finalAnswerOnBudget(lastToolResult) + stats
MaxElapsed path (loop.go:262-273 region) calls gracefulFinalize instead of finalAnswerOnBudget directly
Empty-LLM-response path (loop.go:353-357 region) calls gracefulFinalize instead of inlining finalAnswerOnBudget; sets stats.StopReason = 'empty_llm_response'
MaxIterations exit path (loop.go:629-646 region) refactored to call gracefulFinalize -- same observable behavior as today, just routed through the helper

userStories.title: Budget fallback message includes last-tool context
userStories.description: When the graceful finalize from US-FIX01 fails OR AllowNoToolFinalization is false, today the user sees a single generic string from `finalAnswerOnBudget(lastToolResult)` (loop_dedup.go:79): 'I reached the per-turn budget without a usable result.' Story: enrich the fallback string with (a) which budget hit (max_iterations vs max_elapsed vs empty_llm_response) and (b) the last tool name + iteration count so the user has actionable context. Signature change: `finalAnswerOnBudgetWithContext(lastToolResult string, lastToolName string, stopReason string, opts Options) string`. Examples: max_iterations_hit + last tool 'web_search' + 8 iters -> 'Per-turn step cap reached (8 iterations). Last tool: web_search. Try a more specific request.'; max_elapsed_hit + last tool 'workspace_read' -> 'Per-turn time cap reached (5m0s). Last tool: workspace_read. Try a smaller scope or break it up.'; if zero tools called -> 'Per-turn cap reached without invoking any tool. Try rephrasing -- Aura could not pick a tool for this request.' The lastToolName is available from stats.ToolsCalled (last element). Keep the legacy single-arg `finalAnswerOnBudget` available as a thin wrapper for backward compat (no caller change needed beyond the helper definition).
acceptanceCriteria: internal/agent/loop_dedup.go: new function finalAnswerOnBudgetWithContext(lastToolResult, lastToolName, stopReason, opts) string with the 3 message variants documented above

loop.go call sites in MaxElapsed/MaxIterations/empty-LLM fallback paths (inside gracefulFinalize from US-FIX01) use the new contextual helper, passing the last entry of stats.ToolsCalled + stats.StopReason + opts
Empty-tool-list case ('zero tools called') renders the 'Try rephrasing' variant
Time format: MaxElapsed shows minutes via opts.MaxElapsed.Round(time.Second).String() (e.g., '5m0s'), not raw nanoseconds
